strengths: Novel framework combining explicit persistent 3D state representation with diffusion-based dynamics for interactive world modeling, well-motivated by clear limitations of pixel-only approaches

Comprehensive evaluation combining quantitative metrics (FVD, spatial/temporal consistency), head-to-head user studies (300+ evaluations), and multiple behavioral scenarios with consistent improvements over learned baselines
Solid technical execution with complete pipeline (world frame prediction, camera tracking, world-to-pixel rendering) using appropriate components (flow matching, 3D/2D VAEs)
Excellent experimental design including proper baselines, ablations, calibrated user study protocol, and honest limitations discussion in appendices
Clear presentation with effective visualizations demonstrating that 3D state is actually leveraged for scene editing and consistent geometry maintenance across rollouts
Substantial implementation transparency through detailed algorithms, hyperparameters, and configuration tables enabling reproducibility
weaknesses: Fundamental limitation: requires explicit 3D voxel supervision during training, severely restricting applicability to simulator data; cannot learn from unstructured video alone, as authors acknowledge

No direct 3D geometry evaluation despite being centered on 3D state prediction—missing voxel IoU, depth accuracy, or geometry comparisons to ground truth; evaluation is entirely through 2D metrics and human ratings

Results still substantially below ground truth in user studies (3.0 vs. 3.1 overall score), raising questions about whether explicit 3D representation provides sufficient advantage over implicit methods

Limited scope of evaluation: only synthetic Minecraft environments; no comparison to other 3D world models or 3D-aware video generation approaches; missing computational cost analysis and ablations isolating component contributions

Acknowledged technical issues underexplored: exposure bias during training/inference acknowledged but impact not analyzed; generation glitches regular (Figure 14) without root cause analysis; spatial memory limited to finite region around agent

Incremental technical novelty—combines standard components (flow matching, VAE, diffusion) without introducing new modeling paradigms; individual contributions of each component unclear without proper ablations
Evaluation gaps: no analysis of failure modes, unclear architectural design choices (e.g., why specific voxel resolution, patch sizes), and notation could be clearer in mathematical formulation

strengths: Well-motivated approach addressing genuine limitations of pixel-history methods by substituting with persistent latent 3D representations
Technically sound three-component decomposition (world-frame, camera, pixel) with coherent integration of diffusion models and differentiable rendering

Comprehensive evaluation including quantitative metrics across multiple horizons, human study with 28 participants, and multiple ablations demonstrating clear improvements (PERSIST achieves 148 FVD vs Oasis 875 at 600 frames)
Demonstrates strong long-horizon stability with minimal FID/FVD degradation over 600+ frames while pixel-history baselines fail catastrophically
Clear and honest discussion of limitations with concrete proposals for future work (2D-to-3D foundation models, end-to-end post-training, 3D memory banks)
Excellent reproducibility with extensive implementation details, architectures, hyperparameters, and inference algorithms in appendices
weaknesses: Critical practical limitation: requires ground truth 3D voxel supervision during training, severely restricting applicability to simulators or densely annotated datasets; 2D-to-3D alternative remains undemonstrated
Extremely limited experimental scope restricted to single procedurally-generated voxel environment (Luanti); no evaluation on diverse environments, real-world data, or other platforms

Persistent exposure bias issues remain unresolved despite mitigation attempts—human study shows consistent ground-truth preference across all metrics, and Figure 13 reveals artifacts at steps 672/888/1656 indicating fundamental degradation

Incomplete comparisons: no evaluation against cited 3D-aware methods (Huang et al. 2025a, Voyager, Zhou et al. 2025); human study uses models trained on different domain (Minedojo vs Craftium) potentially biasing results
Inference efficiency inadequate for interactive use (2.67s/frame for PERSIST-S, 0.37 FPS); even with 3× speedup achieves only 0.88s/frame with non-trivial quality loss
Finite spatial memory limitation: world-frame only tracks local region around agent; proposed 3D memory bank solution deferred to future work and not implemented
Insufficient analysis of learned 3D representations: no quantitative evaluation of 3D prediction accuracy, systematic error analysis, or study of what semantic structure is captured
Camera-GT achieves nearly identical FVD (152 vs 141 for base), suggesting camera prediction may be bottleneck, yet this architectural limitation is not explored
World editing and off-screen dynamics capabilities demonstrated only qualitatively without quantitative evaluation or ablation studies

Human study statistical concerns: overlapping error bars, marginal head-to-head improvements (PERSIST-S +0.21 on some metrics), and PERSIST-S performing 'similarly' despite 8× reduction in spatial tokens questions model design efficiency
